book.unit_title: Squares, Square Roots, Cubes and Cube Roots

title: Use of table values and scientific calculator to find square roots
competency: Find square roots of decimals using the table of squares and a calculator.

keywords.def: A table at the end of the book that gives x² for x from 1.00 to 9.99.
If a² = b, then a is a square root of b.

en.text: To find √b from the table of squares, read the table backwards: find b inside the table, slide left to its row (the first two digits) and up to its column (the third digit). If b is not in the table, use the nearest value. Moving the point two places in b moves it one place in √b.

am.text: √b ን ከካሬዎች ሰንጠረዥ ለማግኘት ሰንጠረዡን ወደ ኋላ አንብብ፤ b ን ፈልግ፣ ወደ ግራ ሄደህ ረድፉን፣ ወደ ላይ ሄደህ አምዱን አንብብ።

screens.title: Read the table backwards
screens.after: Square root undoes squaring. If (4.05)² ≈ 16.40, then √16.40 ≈ 4.05. (8.2 is 16.40 ÷ 2: halving is not a square root.)

screens.title: Example 2.12: find √16.40 by reading the table backwards
screens.intro: Forwards: row + column → square. Backwards: square → row + column. Tap ▶.

screens.title: Reading the table backwards
paras: Find the number in the body of the table.
Slide left along its row: the row gives the first two digits.
Slide up its column: the column gives the third digit.
If the number is not in the table, use the nearest one.

screens.title: Key word
defs: A table at the end of the book that gives x² for x from 1.00 to 9.99.

screens.title: Example 2.13: √71.80 is not in the table exactly
screens.intro: 71.80 is between 71.74 and 71.91 in the table. Which is nearer? Tap ▶.

screens.text: Read the table backwards: 98.01 is in row 9.9, column 0. So √98.01 = ?
screens.why:
Row 9.9 gives the first two digits: 9.9.
Column 0 gives the third digit: 0. So x = 9.90.
Check: 9.9 × 9.9 = 98.01. ✓
screens.clue: Row gives the first two digits; column gives the third.

screens.title: Find 12.74 inside the table
screens.ask: Find 12.74 in the table and tap it. Its row and column give √12.74.
screens.clue: Look along the rows 3.5 and 3.6: which cell shows 12.74?

screens.text: Read the table backwards: 11.16 is in row 3.3, column 4. So √11.16 ≈ ?
screens.why:
Row 3.3 → first two digits 3.3.
Column 4 → third digit 4.
So √11.16 ≈ 3.34. Check: 3.34² = 11.1556 ≈ 11.16.
screens.clue: Join the row number and the column digit.

screens.why:
2144 = 21.44 × 100.
√(21.44 × 100) = √21.44 × √100 ≈ 4.63 × 10.
So √2144 ≈ 46.3. The point moved 2 places in the number and 1 place in the root.
screens.clue: Moving the point 2 places in the number moves it 1 place in the root.
Divide by 100 inside the root means divide by 10 outside.

screens.ask: Use a calculator, or try a number: √12.25 = ___

screens.text: (1.52)² ≈ 2.310. Lulit says √231 ≈ 1.52 too. Is she right?
opts: Yes, the digits are the same
screens.why:
231 = 2.310 × 100 (the point moved 2 places).
√(2.310 × 100) = √2.310 × √100 ≈ 1.52 × 10 = 15.2.
Check: 15.2² = 231.04. ✓
Lulit forgot that the point moves too.
screens.clue: How many places did the point move?

So √13.18 ≈ 3.63. Check: 3.63² = 13.1769.

items.clue: Point moves 2 places in the number, 1 place in the root.
